stem: A logistics startup's platform team currently hardcodes the production RDS password inside an environment file that ships with every container image, and the security lead wants the credential rotated automatically every 30 days without any code change. Which approach meets this requirement?

choices.text: Store the password in AWS Secrets Manager and turn on automatic rotation
Store the password as a Systems Manager Parameter Store SecureString parameter and rely on its built-in rotation schedule
Keep the password in the environment file, but restrict which principals can pull the container image
Bake the password into a new AMI every 30 days and redeploy instances from the updated AMI

rationale: AWS Secrets Manager is built to store credentials like a database password and can automatically rotate a supported secret on a schedule by invoking a rotation function, so the application always retrieves the current value at runtime with no code change or redeploy. Parameter Store SecureString values are encrypted with KMS but Parameter Store has no built-in rotation feature, so a rotation schedule cannot be configured there. Restricting who can pull the container image does not remove the hardcoded password from the environment file, so the credential is still exposed to anyone with image access and still is not rotated. Baking the password into a new AMI on a schedule still embeds a long-lived credential in a build artifact, and it requires redeploying instances every cycle, which is exactly the code-change-free rotation the requirement rules out.
